title: OtaconsKeep Continuity Model
honesty: The Continuity Model (CM-01...CM-25) is the design theory for behavioral continuity. Runtime modules implement a subset today (emotional continuity + Formula 5). Worked traces labeled MOCK are synthetic. This page does not claim human consciousness, it claims measurable, bounded state dynamics.
manual_note: The Continuity Model mixes trait ideas, appraisal-style emotion logic, memory scoring, relationship updates, and settle rules. It does not claim human consciousness. It uses simple, grounded math to keep continuity, leftover feeling, social weighting, and context-sensitive behavior over time. The first equations are the behavior engine. The cap and identity equations are the safety layer.
diluted_version: It feels different depending on what happened
Then it decides what to say or do

rationale.title: Why this feels continuous (not conscious)
body: We keep numbers for feelings, bonds, and memory scores between turns. That is the opposite of a blank chat that forgets you.
Multiply when one thing should boost or shrink another. Add when many things all contribute.
Settle rates and baselines pull feelings back toward normal so nothing spirals forever.
Tiny noise stops every reply from sounding identical.
An identity floor keeps the character from dissolving while it adapts.
Chance-stage charts and planning math help analysis. They do not replace the main mood numbers.

core_logic_justification.multiplication: Use multiply when one factor should boost or shrink another (hurt × old wound, praise × trust).
core_logic_justification.summation: Use add when many inputs all count (several events in one turn, many memories competing).
core_logic_justification.decay: Settle terms pull values back toward normal so the agent recovers.
core_logic_justification.bounded_noise: Small noise adds natural variation without chaos.

chapters.title: Trait Weight Model
katex: W_t = B_D \cdot S_t \cdot C_t \cdot P_t \cdot K_t \cdot (1+\varepsilon_t)
chapters.meaning: This turns a written trait into a number. Bigger number = that trait can matter more later.
chapters.why_this_logic: We multiply the pieces together. If one piece is small, the whole strength gets smaller. That way a weak or unsure trait cannot shout as loud as a clear, important one.
chapters.why_these_variables: This is the first step. It makes scores the rest of the math can use.

chapters.title: State Update Model
chapters.meaning: This updates the agent's feeling numbers: add the event hit, add a tiny wiggle, slowly drift back toward normal, then keep the number in range.
chapters.why_this_logic: New feeling = old feeling + capped event change + tiny noise − pull toward baseline. Then we clamp so it stays between allowed limits.
chapters.why_these_variables: This is the heartbeat of mood between Codec turns.

markov_or_notes.body: CM-24 treats stage labels as a Markov chain for analysis and STM diagrams. CM-25 casts goal choice as a constrained utility / goal program. Neither invents PASS results; both are design models for V&V scenarios and planning analysis.

simplified_intro.title: How the Continuity Model fits together
body: Think of an agent like a character that keeps going between messages. It remembers how it feels, whom it trusts, and what mattered before.

The Continuity Model is a stack of small formulas. Early ones score personality traits. Middle ones turn events into mood and relationship changes, then calm things back down. Later ones pick memories, choose goals, and build the reply.
Only some of this is live in code today (mood numbers, blend and settle, comparison events, relationship updates). The rest is the full design, published so the evidence pages match the real model.
Below, every equation is shown first. Right under it is a plain-language walkthrough, with variable cards that use icons and clear names.
